title: Wire role/scopes into config diff access + Sev0/Sev1 break-glass flow
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
release_notes: Config diff endpoint now enforces scoped access (service-to-service + user roles) and supports an audited, time-bounded break-glass flow for Sev0/Sev1 incidents.
body:
Summary: This PR completes the permissioning work for the tenant-aware config diff endpoint by wiring AuthN/AuthZ roles + OAuth scopes into the handler and adding a time-bounded break-glass path for on-call responders during Sev0/Sev1 incidents. The intent is to make incident-bot v2 and Console diagnostics safe-by-default (least privilege, customer-safe output) while still enabling responders to unblock themselves in emergencies with explicit audit trails.

Context: We introduced the config diff endpoint in PR-29112 with redaction hooks and basic authorization plumbing, but we were still relying on coarse environment allowlists. During the 2025-02-07 Hosted API incident followups and INT-3312 we identified gaps: (a) bot lacked a narrowly-scoped permission to call diff in prod, (b) SREs needed a documented break-glass procedure for Sev0/Sev1, and (c) Security required auditable, severity-gated access.

What’s included: 1) Scope + role enforcement: The config service now requires BOTH (i) a service identity scope for machine calls and (ii) a user role for interactive calls. Service-to-service (incident-bot): new scope `configdiff:read_redacted` for customer-safe diffs (redacted + allowlisted fields only). Interactive (Console / CLI): new permission `config.diff.read_redacted` gated by role `platform-oncall` or `sre-oncall` (via Policy Engine). No path returns unredacted diffs via this endpoint. 2) Break-glass for Sev0/Sev1: Added endpoint path `POST /v1/config/diff:breakglass` which returns the same redacted diff but allows bypassing the normal role check when ALL of the following are true: request includes `incident_id`, `severity` in {SEV0, SEV1}, `oncall_user` (from OIDC), and `slack_channel_id` + `slack_thread_ts` for correlation; caller has base scope `breakglass:request` (limited to SRE tooling identities) and is in the on-call group (Pager duty group sync) OR is a member of `sre` org team; break-glass grant is time-bounded (15 minutes) and rate-limited per incident/user. The handler writes a dedicated audit event (see below) and includes a response banner field `breakglass_grant_expires_at` for downstream UI warnings. 3) Policy Engine wiring: Added policy bundle rules to express “standard access” vs “break-glass access” explicitly. This removes the previous env-based branching and makes reviews easier for Security. 4) Audit logging: Emits `audit.config_diff.access` on every request and `audit.breakglass.grant` when break-glass is used (fields: incident_id, severity, tenant_id_hash, actor, client_id, reason, slack_channel_id, slack_thread_ts, grant_ttl_seconds, decision). These align with the audit event schema added in PR-29133. 5) Guardrails: Added per-tenant + per-actor QPS limits for diff reads to prevent incident-bot bursts from amplifying outages. Added a “deny by default” behavior if severity is missing or malformed (no implicit downgrade). All responses include `redaction_applied=true` and omit any raw secret-bearing keys even if present in config state.

Implementation notes: - Auth: Uses Gatekeeper-issued OIDC claims for `actor` and `groups`, plus mTLS client identity for service calls. Bot uses service identity only; user identity is required for interactive. - Tenant handling: Tenant identifier is hashed in audit logs; raw tenant id remains in service logs (restricted) but not in audit event payload. - Redaction: Break-glass does NOT change redaction behavior; it only changes who can retrieve the redacted diff. (Unredacted diff remains an internal-only admin workflow outside of Slack/incident-bot.) - Backwards compat: `GET /v1/config/diff` behavior remains but now enforces policy; callers without the new scope/role will receive `403` with a remediation hint.

Changed areas (high level): - services/config/api/config_diff_handler.go: enforce scopes/roles, add break-glass handler and TTL grant cache. - services/config/authz/policy_rules.rego: new rules for config diff read and break-glass paths. - services/config/audit/audit_events.go: new event emitters + field normalization. - services/config/limits/rate_limits.yaml: per-endpoint budgets for diff and break-glass. - tools/policy-bundle-lint/: updated tests and fixtures.

Commits (squash summary): - Add policy rules + unit tests for config diff read permissions - Add break-glass grant cache w/ TTL and rate limits - Emit audit events for diff access + break-glass grants - Wire new OAuth scopes into service auth middleware - Docs: add operational notes for on-call + security review checklist

Testing / validation: - Unit: config diff handler authz matrix tests (service vs user vs break-glass), redaction invariants, TTL expiry. - Integration: policy bundle evaluation tests in CI. - Manual: verified incident-bot service identity can fetch redacted diffs in staging with new scope; verified non-oncall user receives 403; verified Sev2 with break-glass request denied.

Rollout plan: - Land behind config flag `configdiff.enforce_scopes=true` default false in prod for 24h. - Coordinate with incident-bot scope rollout (ENG-5426) and Console role assignment. - After scopes are deployed, flip to true globally. - Monitor: audit event volume, 403 rates on `/v1/config/diff`, and p95 latency.

Reviewer notes / discussion highlights: - Marcus Lin: requested explicit guarantee that break-glass does not enable unredacted output and that severity gating is deny-by-default. Addressed by keeping shared redaction pipeline and adding strict enum parsing with hard fail. - Kevin Osei: asked for tenant id hashing in audit payload and consistent field names. Updated audit emitter to `tenant_id_hash` and aligned with SIEM pipeline expectations. - Rafael Mendes: asked for on-call usability: clear error messaging for responders + TTL visibility. Added `breakglass_grant_expires_at` and standardized 403 remediation hints (“request break-glass for SEV0/SEV1” + internal runbook link).

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - incident-bot: consume `breakglass_grant_expires_at` and display a warning banner in Slack modal (tracked in ENG-5426). - docs/runbooks: add break-glass SOP + escalation path for Sev0/Sev1 approval (ENG-5431). - security: quarterly access review automation for on-call groups (separate ticket).

Screenshots: N/A (API/policy change only).

Checklist: - [x] Added tests for authz matrix - [x] Added/updated audit events - [x] Verified no unredacted diff path introduced - [x] Added rate limits and deny-by-default severity validation - [x] Coordinated scope name with incident-bot + platform teams
